privacy.ai_training_note: Anyscale is an infrastructure/compute platform, not a foundation-model trainer on customer workloads. Its Privacy Notice does not apply to Customer Data (the customer remains controller of data processed in their own clusters). Anyscale states it may use Usage Data to develop, improve, support, and operate its products and services, which is operational telemetry, not training models on customer datasets or code. No evidence of training on customer business data by default. A DPA and Data Security Addendum are referenced as part of the agreement, with a Supplemental Notice for EU/UK GDPR.
privacy.data_region: Dual-plane architecture: the Customer Data Plane (where customer data and workloads run) executes inside the customer's own cloud account or Kubernetes cluster (AWS, GCP, Azure) via Bring-Your-Own-Cloud, so sensitive data stays in the customer's VPC. Only orchestration metadata flows to the Anyscale Control Plane. Application logs and customer data are stored locally on the cluster; ingested logs for the log viewer are opt-in by default for Anyscale Hosted clouds. Subprocessors are US-based (AWS, Google, Microsoft, Pylon) with Tailscale in Canada.

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: Yes. Third-party penetration test conducted; 2025 executive summary available via trust center on request.

security.name: Vulnerability disclosure
security.value: Trust center provides a 'Report a vulnerability' channel and trust@anyscale.com. No public HackerOne/Bugcrowd bug-bounty program found.

security.name: Encryption
security.value: Encryption in transit and at rest using industry-standard algorithms; managed key lifecycle; encrypted backups; server certificate authentication.

security.name: Access control
security.value: Role-based access control, least privilege, quarterly logical access reviews, password policy enforcement, onboarding/offboarding workflows. SSO, SAML, SCIM, and audit logs for enterprise governance.

security.name: Infrastructure security
security.value: Network segmentation, firewall with default deny, intrusion detection system, immutable infrastructure deployments, automated capacity monitoring.

security.name: Dedicated security team
security.value: Anyscale states it has a dedicated internal security team with documented controls and policies.

products.name: Anyscale Platform (Hosted)
products.category: Managed AI compute / distributed training & inference
products.data_scope: Anyscale-hosted control and data plane; log ingestion opt-in by default; covered by SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001.
products.notes: Fastest onboarding; suited to teams without strict data-residency constraints. Free tier with $100 credit available.

products.name: Anyscale Bring-Your-Own-Cloud (BYOC)
products.category: Self-managed data plane in customer VPC
products.data_scope: Customer Data Plane runs inside the customer's own AWS/GCP/Azure account or Kubernetes cluster; data does not leave the customer network perimeter. Only orchestration metadata reaches the Anyscale Control Plane.
products.notes: Preferred for regulated/enterprise workloads needing data residency and isolation. Supports EC2/VM, EKS, SageMaker HyperPod, GKE/Kubernetes.

products.name: Ray (open source)
products.data_scope: Self-hosted; runs entirely in the user's own environment; no Anyscale data processing.
products.notes: Foundation that Anyscale commercializes; 500M+ downloads, 41K+ GitHub stars. No vendor compliance scope since it is self-operated.

compare.pricing_model: Usage-based (compute consumption) with a free tier / $100 starting credit; enterprise contracts via sales. Available on AWS Marketplace.
compare.data_residency: Customer-controlled via BYOC (data plane in customer's own cloud/K8s); US-based subprocessors for hosted control plane.

flags: No public bug-bounty platform (HackerOne/Bugcrowd); disclosure handled via trust center contact only.
Cert artifacts (SOC 2 report, ISO certificate, pen test summary) are gated behind 'Request access' on the trust center, not publicly downloadable.
Hosted-cloud log ingestion is opt-in by default, so customers using the hosted plane should review log-data flow to the control plane.
